entities.name: Anti-Phishing Working Group
entities.description: The Anti-Phishing Working Group (APWG) describes its work as unifying the global response to cybercrime through curated data exchange, research, public policy, and awareness. It convenes the annual Symposium on Electronic Crime Research (eCrime) and operates the eCrime eXchange.

points_of_contact.name: APWG Accounts
points_of_contact.title: Account information published on the eCX page

capabilities.name: eCrime eXchange (eCX)
capabilities.summary: Member clearinghouse for cybercrime event data, with a REST API and a web interface.
capabilities.description: APWG describes eCrime eXchange as a clearinghouse for cybercrime event data, operating since 2004. The provider states that members contribute and retrieve phishing URLs, phishing email content, malicious IP addresses, maliciously registered domain names, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and malicious SMS or text-message metadata. The same page says eCX offers a RESTful API and a web UI, that records carry confidence scores and provenance, and that the exchange is agreement-based rather than a public open feed.

usage_restrictions: The provider states that eCX is available to APWG members and is governed by its data-sharing agreement.
The provider states that the exchange is not a public open feed.

related_publications.title: Practical API Integration: Connecting Applications to the eCrimex eXchange Data Clearinghouse
APWG eCrime eXchange Preview & Update
PhishFarm: A Scalable Framework for Measuring the Effectiveness of Evasion Techniques Against Browser Phishing Blacklists
related_publications.venue: IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy

entities.name: The Spamhaus Project
entities.description: The Spamhaus Project describes itself as a nonprofit that publishes signal and intelligence about Internet identifiers, including DNS blocklists used to filter email. It is registered in Andorra. Spamhaus Technology is a separate licensee of abuse.ch data; the abuse.ch platforms are catalogued under their own record.

capabilities.name: Spamhaus DNS Blocklists
capabilities.summary: DNS blocklists of IPs and domains associated with spam, phishing, malware, and policy violations.
capabilities.description: Spamhaus publishes DNS blocklists for mail filtering. Its blocklist page names the Spamhaus Blocklist (SBL), Exploits Blocklist (XBL), Policy Blocklist (PBL), Domain Blocklist (DBL), and Combined Spam Sources (CSS). Queries are made from mail servers and filtering tools. The provider says a public query service still exists but is being deprecated, and that Spamhaus Technology offers a free service with published usage criteria.

access.authentication: DNS query; see provider usage criteria
usage_restrictions: The provider states that the public DNSBL query service is subject to a fair-use policy and is being deprecated.
Current access terms are the provider's DNSBL usage criteria, which were not copied into this record.

capabilities.name: Phishing campaign domain clustering
capabilities.summary: eCrime 2026 training on investigating phishing campaigns by clustering domains.
capabilities.description: The APWG eCrime 2026 program lists a training session, Amplify the Signal: Investigating phishing campaigns through domain clustering, presented by Sven Krohlas and affiliated with Spamhaus-abuse.ch. This record does not confirm a software release, dataset, or access method for that work.

related_publications.title: Amplify the Signal: Investigating phishing campaigns through domain clustering

entities.name: abuse.ch
entities.description: abuse.ch is an independent, community-driven malware and botnet intelligence project. Its site says the platforms are free and operated together with Spamhaus. A project post states that on 1 August 2022 Spamhaus Technology became the primary licensee of data produced by abuse.ch.

capabilities.name: URLhaus
capabilities.summary: Community exchange of URLs used to distribute malware.
capabilities.description: URLhaus is a platform from abuse.ch and Spamhaus for sharing malicious URLs used in malware distribution. The project page invites people to browse the database, report URLs, and use an API for bulk queries. Current account and reuse terms are published by the operator and were not copied here.

usage_restrictions: The operator describes the platform as a community exchange. Current API and account terms were not independently copied into this record.

capabilities.name: MalwareBazaar
capabilities.summary: Community collection of malware samples for research and detection.
capabilities.description: MalwareBazaar is a platform from abuse.ch and Spamhaus for sharing malware samples with the security community, antivirus vendors, and threat-intelligence providers. The project page describes browsing the collection, uploading samples, alerts, and an API.

usage_restrictions: Samples are malicious software. The operator's current sharing and API terms were not copied into this record.

capabilities.name: ThreatFox
capabilities.summary: Community exchange of malware indicators of compromise.
capabilities.description: ThreatFox is a platform from abuse.ch and Spamhaus for sharing indicators of compromise associated with malware. The project page describes browsing indicators, contributing indicators, and an API.

usage_restrictions: The operator's current API and account terms were not copied into this record.

capabilities.name: YARAify
capabilities.summary: Scan files against a community repository of YARA rules.
capabilities.description: YARAify is a platform from abuse.ch and Spamhaus for scanning suspicious files and process dumps against a large repository of YARA rules. The project page also describes alerts, an API, and sharing rules through YARAhub. The YARAhub address was not copied because it was not captured as a stable URL in the source reviewed for this record.

usage_restrictions: The operator's current API and account terms were not copied into this record.

entities.name: The Shadowserver Foundation
entities.description: The Shadowserver Foundation says it provides timely Internet security data at no charge, including daily remediation reports for network owners and national response teams, plus support for investigations.

capabilities.name: Shadowserver network reporting
capabilities.summary: Free daily remediation reports for vetted network owners and response teams.
capabilities.description: Shadowserver states that it sends daily custom remediation reports to more than 10,000 vetted subscribers, including national CSIRTs, and that an API is available after requesting a key. The provider says the underlying observations come from Internet-wide scans, sinkholes, honeypot sensors, sandboxes, and blocklists. It also says API helper scripts and a report manager are published on its GitHub page; that repository URL was not copied into this record.

usage_restrictions: The provider states that reports are free for vetted subscribers and are meant for the recipient's remediation and defense.

related_publications.title: Why Is Law Enforcement Being Dominated by Sub-domains?

entities.name: ChongLuaDao
entities.description: ChongLuaDao (Chống Lừa Đảo) is a Vietnam-based social enterprise focused on protecting people from online fraud and phishing. Its about page says it offers free community tools to check suspicious content, report harmful sites, and receive alerts. The legal entity named on that page is ChongLuaDao Social Enterprise Company Limited, directed by Ngô Minh Hiếu (also known there as Hieu Ngo and Hieu PC).

capabilities.name: Scam website detection
capabilities.summary: Free browser-based warnings for scam and phishing sites aimed at Vietnamese users.
capabilities.description: ChongLuaDao's about page says a browser extension released in 2021 warns users about scam websites, combining crowdsourced reports, expert review, and machine learning. The page also says the project has contributed data to APWG since 2021. A specific extension-store listing was not copied into this record.

capabilities.name: Threat lookup
capabilities.summary: Public lookup for suspicious links, messages, and images.
capabilities.description: ChongLuaDao's about page says that in 2022 it introduced an online threat lookup tool and a Telegram chatbot so people can check suspicious links, messages, and images. This record does not publish a separate tool URL because the about page did not state one.

capabilities.name: Scam-camp indicator exchange model
capabilities.summary: eCrime 2026 session on an indicator exchange for earlier intervention.
capabilities.description: The APWG eCrime 2026 program lists Scam Camps Signal Before They Scale: Building an Indicator Exchange Model for Preemptive Intervention, presented by Hieu Minh Ngo and Quynh Nhu Nguyen of ChongLuaDao. The program marks the session as a video presentation. This record does not confirm that an indicator exchange is available for outside use.

related_publications.title: Scam Camps Signal Before They Scale: Building an Indicator Exchange Model for Preemptive Intervention

entities.name: Global Signal Exchange
entities.description: The Global Signal Exchange (GSE) describes itself as a UK nonprofit collaboration, powered with Oxford Information Labs, for sharing scam and fraud signals among trusted organizations. Its about page names Emily Taylor, Lucien Taylor, and Mark Robertshaw as co-founders and says participants can share data bilaterally, anonymously, or in aggregated form.

capabilities.name: Global Signal Exchange platform
capabilities.summary: Trusted exchange for scam and fraud signals, including API access for participants.
capabilities.description: GSE describes a platform where trusted parties share abuse and fraud signals. Public feature descriptions include private sharing groups, API access for participants, and access to threat-intelligence feeds available to those participants. Who may join, and under what agreement, is not restated here.

usage_restrictions: The provider describes participation as limited to trusted parties.

capabilities.name: GSE Compass
capabilities.summary: Provider tool for charts, reports, and threat-intelligence insights on GSE data.
capabilities.description: The GSE website describes Compass as its tool for producing threat-intelligence insights, charts, and reports. This record does not restate third-party descriptions of how queries are written. Access follows participation in the exchange, which this registry has not reconfirmed.

usage_restrictions: Described by the provider as part of the trusted exchange.

entities.name: Oxford Information Labs
entities.description: Oxford Information Labs (OXIL) describes itself as a cyber-intelligence consultancy working on security, resilience, and Internet-governance policy. Its site says OXIL Research is the nonprofit research arm. OXIL is also a founder of the Global Signal Exchange, which is catalogued separately.

capabilities.name: Rethinking Scam Prevention
capabilities.summary: Two-year research project on who scams target and how safeguarding might respond.
capabilities.description: OXIL lists Rethinking Scam Prevention as an active 2026–2027 project. The project page says it studies how scams target adult populations, using the lab's figure of AI-driven analysis of 70 million threat signals, and aims at a safeguarding approach. Alice Taylor is listed to present related work at APWG eCrime 2026. This record does not confirm a dataset or service that outside parties can query.

related_publications.title: Rethinking Scam Prevention: Safeguarding Adults Against Scams and Fraud

entities.name: BforeAI
entities.description: BforeAI, also presented on its public site as Bfore, describes PreCrime as a commercial predictive-security platform. The eCrime 2026 program lists a PreCrime Labs at BforeAI case study. Performance figures on the marketing site were not independently checked.

capabilities.name: PreCrime
capabilities.summary: Commercial platform the provider says identifies malicious infrastructure before campaigns go live.
capabilities.description: BforeAI's website describes PreCrime as a platform that looks for malicious infrastructure, phishing, impersonation, and related preparations before a campaign is active. The eCrime 2026 program lists Abu Bakr Qureshi, PreCrime Labs at BforeAI, on a case study of domain abuse around a large event. This registry has not confirmed an API, a trial process, or the provider's performance claims.

usage_restrictions: Commercial offering. A public request process and contract terms were not copied into this record.

related_publications.title: Prediction at Scale, Confirmation at the Margin: A Case Study in Mega-Event Domain Abuse

entities.name: Interisle Consulting Group
entities.description: Interisle Consulting Group publishes measurement studies of phishing, malware, spam, and the domain-name resources used in those attacks. It publishes the Cybercrime Information Center, a public repository of those studies and of activity tables. Dave Piscitello and Greg Aaron are listed to present Cybercrime Supply Chain 2026 at APWG eCrime 2026.

capabilities.name: Cybercrime Supply Chain studies
capabilities.summary: Annual public measurements of resources used in malware, phishing, and spam.
capabilities.description: The Cybercrime Information Center, published by Interisle, describes Cybercrime Supply Chain 2026 as a study of where criminals obtain attack resources, following earlier editions in the same series. A direct report file was not identified for this record. Separate phishing, malware, and spam activity tables are listed in the Center's records repository.

related_publications.title: Cybercrime Supply Chain 2026: Measurements and Assessments of Cyber Attack Resources and Where Criminals Acquire Them
Cybercrime Supply Chain 2026

capabilities.name: Cybercrime Information Center records
capabilities.summary: Public activity tables for phishing, malware, and spam.
capabilities.description: The Cybercrime Information Center describes itself as a repository of studies, measurements, data sets, and statistics on threats that use the Domain Name System and Internet numbering systems. Its records repository lists phishing, malware, and spam activity tables by top-level domain, registrar, and hosting network. The tables are published for investigators and researchers to use. File formats, a license, and an API were not identified for this record.

capabilities.name: Phishing Landscape
capabilities.summary: Annual public study of where phishing is hosted and which resources it uses.
capabilities.description: Interisle's homepage describes Phishing Landscape 2025 as its fifth annual study of the scope and distribution of phishing. Individual authors and a direct report file were not identified on the page reviewed for this record.

related_publications.title: Phishing Landscape 2025: An Annual Study of the Scope and Distribution of Phishing

entities.name: ISECOM
entities.description: ISECOM, the Institute for Security and Open Methodologies, describes itself as an open security-research institute established in 2001, with roots in Barcelona and New York. It publishes the OSSTMM and the Hacker Highschool education project. Pete Herzog is listed at eCrime 2026 for a threat-modeling training and an OSSTMM session.

capabilities.name: OSSTMM
capabilities.summary: Open methodology for operational security testing, analysis, and trust measurement.
capabilities.description: ISECOM describes the Open Source Security Testing Methodology Manual (OSSTMM) as its public security-testing methodology, with materials available for download and further resources offered through membership. This record treats it as a published method, not as a hosted detection service or data feed. License terms were not copied from the manual.

usage_restrictions: The provider offers public OSSTMM materials and additional resources through membership.

related_publications.title: OSSTMM, Mr. Crimebot and Me: Assessing the AAMs That Assess Our Cybercrime Resilience

entities.name: Operation Shamrock
entities.description: Operation Shamrock is a nonprofit founded by Erin West. Its public materials describe a mission to educate, mobilize, and disrupt transnational scam operations, with emphasis on cryptocurrency investment fraud. A public statement by the founder describes the organization as a 501(c)(3).

capabilities.name: Scam disruption coalition
capabilities.summary: Cross-sector education and disruption work on cryptocurrency investment scams.
capabilities.description: Operation Shamrock publicly describes education, mobilization of law enforcement and industry, and disruption of transnational scam operations. A March 2026 public statement by the founder also describes training for financial institutions and a victim-triage partnership with TRM Labs. This registry has not verified a machine-readable feed, an API, or a data-sharing agreement. Erin West is listed on the eCrime 2026 program for a video presentation on this disruption work.

related_publications.title: West on Pigbutchering Disruption

UNCW's scholars profile lists her as a presenter. The symposium schedule lists Abhishek Satyam of Fordham University for that session. This record does not claim a university-operated service.

capabilities.name: Strategic Agentic Scambaiting
capabilities.summary: eCrime 2026 formal model of defensive agents interacting with scam agents.
capabilities.description: The APWG eCrime 2026 accepted-paper roll describes The Promise of Strategic Agentic Scambaiting as a formal model of agent-to-agent fraud interactions. Named authors are Abhishek Satyam and Juntao Chen (Fordham University), Hossein Siadati (Cybera Global), Haadi Jafarian (University of Colorado Denver), and Sima Jafarikhah (University of North Carolina Wilmington). The public abstract discusses modeled conditions for defensive scambaiting. A project page is listed at https://ai-scambaiting.pages.dev/. No dataset or access method was identified for this record.
